# plainly

> plainly is a dependency-free pytest plugin and assertion library for Python (3.9+, MIT). Every test check is written and reported as one plain-English sentence, such as "fib(-1) should raise ValueError", so humans can review AI-written unit tests quickly. It saves the sentences to a SPEC.md file that is committed with the tests, and its plainly-diff command flags pull requests that remove or loosen a check.

Use plainly when you write or review Python unit tests and want the behaviour they promise to be readable without opening the test code. Typical uses: reviewing tests generated by AI coding agents, test-first development where tests are the contract, and PR review of test changes.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/plainly-dev/plainly-python/blob/main/README.md): full guide with examples, report formats and the API table
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/plainly-dev/plainly-python/blob/main/AGENTS.md): repository layout, commands and rules for AI agents contributing to plainly
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/plainly-dev/plainly-python/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): how to contribute

## API summary

- `expect(value).should.be(x)` / `.must.be(x)` / `.should.not_.be(x)`, plus `greater_than`, `less_than`, `between`, `close_to`, `contain`, `have_length`, `match`, `instance_of`, `one_of`, `satisfy(pred, "description")`
- `calling(f, *args).should.raise_(ValueError, message="text")` and `.should.return_(x)`: defers the call so exceptions are checked
- `spec(f).if_(*args).then_give(y)` / `.then_raise(E)` / `.then_warn(W)`: many examples of one function as "if this, then that" rules
- `given(Class, **kwargs)`: a story of steps on an object that changes, checked with `.then.holds(...)`, `.holds_keys(...)`, `.lacks(...)`, `.has(...)`
- `pytest --plainly`: print the sentences; `--plainly-md SPEC.md`: write them; `--plainly-check SPEC.md`: fail in CI if SPEC.md is out of date
- `plainly-diff --base origin/main SPEC.md [--fail-on-weakened]`: Markdown report of removed, loosened and changed checks
- `plainly-lint tests/`: list bare `assert` and `pytest.raises` in test files (exit 1 if any); `# plainly: allow` keeps a line

## Examples

- [examples/test_fibonacci.py](https://github.com/plainly-dev/plainly-python/blob/main/examples/test_fibonacci.py): small demo
- [examples/spec-review.yml](https://github.com/plainly-dev/plainly-python/blob/main/examples/spec-review.yml): GitHub workflow that comments plainly-diff on PRs
- [case-studies/](https://github.com/plainly-dev/plainly-python/tree/main/case-studies): humanize, python-semver and cachetools test suites rewritten with plainly, and tests written first for a small Flask CRM that is not built yet
